verdict: WEAK - no error tracking and no structured logging

findings.title: No error tracking service
findings.evidence: sentry/sentry-laravel is absent from composer.json (0 matches).
findings.impact: Unhandled exceptions in production produce no alert and no aggregated diagnostic context.

findings.title: No structured JSON log channel
findings.evidence: config/logging.php has no 'json' channel; the stack defaults to LOG_STACK=single.
findings.impact: Logs are unstructured single files, which makes aggregation, querying and retention management difficult.

findings.title: LOG_LEVEL=debug
findings.impact: Debug-level logging in a request path is verbose, increases disk usage and may log more detail than intended. Must be info/warning in production.

findings.title: No request-correlation or trace identifiers
findings.evidence: No middleware attaches a request id to the log context.
findings.impact: A single user action that fans out across use cases, events, listeners and notifications cannot be reconstructed from logs.

findings.title: No health-check endpoint
findings.evidence: No /up or equivalent health route exposing DB/queue/cache reachability.
findings.impact: An orchestrator cannot distinguish an application failure from a dependency failure.

present: Laravel's default log stack, daily/single/stderr channels available via env.
ActivityLog model and listeners exist for domain-level audit trails (a genuine strength, though distinct from operational observability).
changes_made: None. Adding a logging channel or a dependency changes deployment surface, so it is recommended rather than applied.
